title: What do the key consumer configs do: `enable.auto.commit` (auto vs manual offset commit, and why manual + commit-after-processing gives at-least-once), `auto.offset.reset` (`earliest` vs `latest` when there is no committed offset), `max.poll.records` (max records per `poll()`, not a total cap), and `max.poll.interval.ms` (too-slow processing between polls triggers a rebalance)?
shortTitle: What do the key consumer configs do?

s1_definition.oneliner: enable.auto.commit controls safe manual commit for at-least-once, auto.offset.reset picks backlog versus skip for a fresh group, max.poll.records sizes each poll batch, and max.poll.interval.ms evicts a consumer that processes a batch too slowly.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **enable.auto.commit** -- when true (default), offsets commit on a timer; when false, you commit manually after processing, giving clean at-least-once delivery.
- **auto.offset.reset** -- decides where a consumer starts when there is no committed offset: `earliest` reads the whole backlog, `latest` skips to the end, `none` throws an error.
- **max.poll.records** -- caps how many records a single `poll()` returns (default 500); it is a per-batch limit, not a total consumption cap.
- **max.poll.interval.ms** -- bounds the time allowed between successive `poll()` calls (default 5 minutes); exceeding it triggers a rebalance because the coordinator assumes the consumer is stalled.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of a settlement clerk at National Bank of India. The auto-commit setting is whether the clerk marks slips cleared automatically on a timer or only after actually doing the work. The offset-reset setting is, for a brand-new clerk, whether they begin from the oldest slip in the tray or only from slips arriving after they sit down. The max-poll-records setting is how many slips the clerk grabs in one handful. And the max-poll-interval setting is the rule that if the clerk takes too long before grabbing the next handful, the supervisor assumes they are stuck and reassigns their tray.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
 Consumer Config Decision Flow
 ==============================

 ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
 │        Consumer Starts Up            │
 └──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                │
                ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Does a committed offset exist?       │
 └───────┬─────────────────┬───────────┘
    yes  │                 │  no
         ▼                 ▼
 ┌───────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────┐
 │ Resume from   │  │ auto.offset.reset?       │
 │ committed     │  ├─────────┬───────┬───────┤
 │ offset        │  │earliest │latest │ none  │
 └───────────────┘  │         │       │       │
                    ▼         ▼       ▼
              ┌─────────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌───────┐
              │ Read all│ │ Skip │ │ Throw │
              │ backlog │ │ old  │ │ error │
              └─────────┘ └──────┘ └───────┘


 Poll Loop Timing
 ================

  poll() ──► process batch ──► commitSync() ──► poll()
    │                                             │
    │◄──────── max.poll.interval.ms ─────────────►│
    │                                             │
    │   batch size = max.poll.records (default 500)
    │
    │   If processing takes > max.poll.interval.ms:
    │     Coordinator evicts consumer → rebalance
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
These four consumer settings control correctness, startup behavior, and liveness. The auto-commit setting decides whether offsets commit on a timer or manually. For clean at-least-once I disable auto-commit and commit only after processing succeeds, so a crash before commit causes a safe reprocess rather than a loss.

The offset-reset setting only matters for a brand-new group: earliest reads the whole backlog, latest starts at the end. The max-poll-records setting caps each poll batch, and the max-poll-interval bounds the time between polls, evicting a consumer that processes too slowly.

In my National Bank of India fraud-scoring consumer, I set reset to earliest for the full backlog, disabled auto-commit, lowered max-poll-records so each batch finished inside the poll interval, and the consumer was safe, complete, and stable.

Remember one sentence: disable auto-commit for safety, set earliest for completeness, size max-poll-records for your processing speed, and keep each batch inside the poll interval to avoid eviction.

---

keyPoints: enable.auto.commit=false gives clean at-least-once by committing only after processing succeeds.
auto.offset.reset=earliest reads the full backlog for a new group; latest silently skips existing messages.
max.poll.records caps per-poll batch size (default 500) and is not a total consumption limit.
max.poll.interval.ms evicts a consumer that takes too long between polls, triggering a rebalance.
auto.offset.reset is irrelevant when a committed offset already exists; the consumer resumes there.
Size max.poll.records so each batch finishes processing within the max.poll.interval.ms window.
